metadata.title: Strong Convergence of the Empirical Distribution of Eigenvalues of Large Dimensional Random Matrices
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: Empirical Distribution Function of Eigenvalues
nodes.statement: For any square matrix $A$ with only real eigenvalues, $F^A$ denotes the empirical distribution function (e.d.f.) of the eigenvalues of $A$, i.e. $F^A(x)$ is the proportion of eigenvalues of $A$ that are $\leq x$.
nodes.statement_clean: F^A(x) is the empirical distribution function of the eigenvalues of A.

nodes.name: Stieltjes Transform
nodes.statement: For any p.d.f. $G$, the Stieltjes transform is the analytic function $m_G(z) \equiv \int \frac{1}{\lambda - z}\, dG(\lambda)$ for $z \in \mathbb{C}^+ \equiv \{z \in \mathbb{C} : \mathrm{Im}\, z > 0\}$.
nodes.statement_clean: m_G(z) is the integral of 1/(lambda - z) against G, defined on the upper half plane.

nodes.name: Stieltjes Inversion Formula
nodes.statement: $G\{[a,b]\} = \frac{1}{\pi}\lim_{\eta \to 0^+} \int_a^b \mathrm{Im}\, m_G(\xi + i\eta)\, d\xi$, valid at continuity points $a,b$ of $G$.
nodes.statement_clean: Recovers the measure G on continuity intervals from the imaginary part of its Stieltjes transform.

nodes.name: Stieltjes Transform via Resolvent
nodes.statement: For $p \times p$ matrix $A$ with real eigenvalues $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_p$: $m_{F^A}(z) = (1/p)\sum_{i=1}^p \frac{1}{\lambda_i - z} = (1/p)\,\mathrm{tr}\,(A - zI)^{-1}$.
nodes.statement_clean: The Stieltjes transform of an empirical spectral distribution equals (1/p) times the trace of the resolvent.

nodes.name: Marcenko-Pastur Equation
nodes.statement: $m = -\Bigl(z - c\int \frac{\tau\, dH(\tau)}{1 + \tau m}\Bigr)^{-1}$, where $m = m_{\underline{F}}(z)$ for $z \in \mathbb{C}^+$ and the solution is unique in $\mathbb{C}^+$.
nodes.statement_clean: Defining equation (1.1) for the Stieltjes transform of the limit of (1/N)X*TX.

nodes.name: Spectra Relation Between (1/N)X*TX and (1/N)XX*T
nodes.statement: $F^{(1/N)X^* T X} = (1 - n/N)\, I_{[0,\infty)} + (n/N)\, F^{(1/N) X X^* T}$, equating their e.d.f.'s up to $|n - N|$ zero eigenvalues.
nodes.statement_clean: The two matrix products differ in spectrum only by |n-N| zero eigenvalues.

nodes.name: Stieltjes Transform Identity (1.2)
nodes.statement: $m_{F^{(1/N)X^* T X}}(z) = -\frac{(1 - n/N)}{z} + \frac{n}{N}\, m_{F^{(1/N) X X^* T}}(z)$ for $z \in \mathbb{C}^+$.
nodes.statement_clean: Identity relating the Stieltjes transforms of the two related matrix products.

nodes.name: Limit Stieltjes Transform Identity (1.3)
nodes.statement: $m_{\underline{F}}(z) = -\frac{(1 - c)}{z} + c\, m_F(z)$ for $z \in \mathbb{C}^+$.
nodes.statement_clean: Limiting form of (1.2) relating the Stieltjes transforms of F and underline-F.

nodes.name: Defining Equation (1.4) for $m_F$
nodes.statement: $m = \int \frac{1}{\tau(1 - c - czm) - z}\, dH(\tau)$, with uniqueness in $\{m \in \mathbb{C} : -\frac{(1-c)}{z} + cm \in \mathbb{C}^+\}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Equation (1.4): unique-in-D_c equation characterizing the limit Stieltjes transform m_F(z).

nodes.name: Standing Assumptions on $X$, $T$, $n/N$
nodes.statement: (a) $X_n = (X_{ij}^n)$ is $n \times N$ with $X_{ij}^n \in \mathbb{C}$, i.d. for all $n,i,j$, independent across $i,j$ for each $n$, $E|X_{11}^1 - EX_{11}^1|^2 = 1$. (b) $N = N(n)$ with $n/N \to c > 0$. (c) $T_n$ is $n\times n$ random Hermitian non-negative definite, $F^{T_n}\to H$ a.s. on $[0,\infty)$. (d) $X_n$ and $T_n$ are independent.
nodes.statement_clean: Standing conditions (a)-(d) on the random matrix entries, the dimension ratio, and the deterministic spectral limit of T.

nodes.name: Theorem 1.1 (Strong Convergence of $F^{B_n}$)
nodes.statement: Under assumptions (a)-(d), with $B_n = (1/N)\, T_n^{1/2} X_n X_n^* T_n^{1/2}$, almost surely $F^{B_n}$ converges in distribution to a nonrandom p.d.f. $F$ whose Stieltjes transform $m(z)$ is the unique solution in $D_c \equiv \{m \in \mathbb{C} : -\frac{(1-c)}{z} + cm \in \mathbb{C}^+\}$ of equation (1.4).
nodes.statement_clean: Almost surely, F^{B_n} converges to a deterministic limit F whose Stieltjes transform satisfies (1.4) uniquely in D_c.
assumptions: $X_n$ has i.d. complex entries with $E|X_{11}-EX_{11}|^2 = 1$, independent across $(i,j)$
$T_n$ is $n\times n$ random Hermitian non-negative definite, $F^{T_n} \to H$ a.s. on $[0,\infty)$
conclusions: Almost surely $F^{B_n}$ converges in distribution to a nonrandom p.d.f. $F$
The Stieltjes transform $m(z)$ of $F$ is the unique solution in $D_c$ of equation (1.4)

nodes.name: Sherman-Morrison-Type Identity (2.1)
nodes.statement: For $n \times n$ $B$ and $q \in \mathbb{C}^n$ with $B$ and $B + qq^*$ invertible: $q^* (B + qq^*)^{-1} = \frac{1}{1 + q^* B^{-1} q}\, q^* B^{-1}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Rank-one perturbation identity used throughout the proof.

nodes.name: Lemma 2.1 (Quadratic-Form Concentration)
nodes.statement: Let $C$ be $n \times n$ with $\|C\| \leq 1$ and $Y = (X_1,\dots,X_n)^T$ with i.i.d. $X_i$ satisfying conditions (1) and (2). Then $E|Y^* C Y - \mathrm{tr}\, C|^6 \leq K n^3 \log^{12} n$, where $K$ does not depend on $n$, $C$, or the distribution of $X_1$.
nodes.statement_clean: Sixth-moment bound on the deviation of a quadratic form Y*CY from its expectation tr C.
assumptions: $Y = (X_1,\dots,X_n)^T$ with i.i.d. entries satisfying truncation/centralization (1) and (2)
conclusions: $E|Y^* C Y - \mathrm{tr}\, C|^6 \leq K n^3 \log^{12} n$ with universal constant $K$

nodes.name: Lemma 2.2 (Trace Perturbation Bound)
nodes.statement: Let $z \in \mathbb{C}^+$ with $v = \mathrm{Im}\, z$, $A,B$ $n \times n$ with $B$ Hermitian, and $q \in \mathbb{C}^n$. Then $\bigl|\mathrm{tr}\,((B - zI)^{-1} - (B + \tau q q^* - zI)^{-1}) A\bigr| \leq \|A\|/v$.
nodes.statement_clean: Bound on the trace difference between resolvents of B and a rank-one perturbation B + tau qq*.

nodes.name: Lemma 2.3 (Resolvent Inequalities for $(m(z)A + I)^{-1}$)
nodes.statement: For $z = u + iv \in \mathbb{C}^+$, $m_1, m_2$ Stieltjes transforms of p.d.f.'s, $A,B$ $n\times n$ with $A$ Hermitian non-negative definite, $r \in \mathbb{C}^n$: (a) $\|(m_1(z)A + I)^{-1}\| \leq \max(4\|A\|/v, 2)$; (b) $|\mathrm{tr}\, B((m_1 A+I)^{-1} - (m_2 A+I)^{-1})| \leq |m_2 - m_1|\, n\|B\|\|A\|\,(\max(4\|A\|/v,2))^2$; (c) $|r^* B(m_1 A+I)^{-1} r - r^* B(m_2 A+I)^{-1} r| \leq |m_2-m_1|\,\|r\|^2 \|B\|\|A\|\,(\max(4\|A\|/v,2))^2$.
nodes.statement_clean: Three operator-norm and trace inequalities controlling differences of (m_i A + I)^{-1} as m_i varies.
assumptions: $m_1(z), m_2(z)$ are Stieltjes transforms of p.d.f.'s
$A$ is $n\times n$ Hermitian non-negative definite; $B$ is $n\times n$; $r \in \mathbb{C}^n$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.3
nodes.statement: Notice (b) and (c) follow from (a) by basic matrix manipulations; (a) follows by reducing $|m_1(z)x + 1|^2 = (\mathrm{Re}\, m_1 x + 1)^2 + (\mathrm{Im}\, m_1)^2 x^2$ via Cauchy-Schwarz to minimizing $f(y) = a y^4 + (y+1)^2$ with $a = (v/x)^2$, yielding $f(y) \geq \min(a/16, 1/4)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Proof reduces (b) and (c) to (a); proves (a) by minimizing a quartic-plus-quadratic lower envelope.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.1
nodes.statement: Truncate and centralize entries of $X$ and eigenvalues of $T$ via Silverstein-Bai [2]; then use the resolvent identity (2.1), tightness of $\{F^{B_n}\}$, Lemmas 2.1-2.3, and (2.5)-(2.6) to show $\frac{1}{n}\,\mathrm{tr}\,(-z\underline{m}_n(z)T_n - zI)^{-1} - \underline{m}_n(z) \to 0$ a.s., extract a convergent subsequence, and use uniqueness in $D_c$ to conclude $\underline{m}_n(z) \to \underline{m}$ where $m$ satisfies (1.4).
nodes.statement_clean: Truncate-centralize, apply resolvent identity, derive bounds via Lemmas 2.1-2.3, extract limit, use uniqueness.

nodes.name: Truncation and Centralization of $X$ and $T$
nodes.statement: Through two successive truncations and centralizations of $X$ (at $\pm \sqrt{N}$ then at $\pm \ln N$) and a final scaling, plus eigenvalue truncation $T \mapsto T_\alpha = U \mathrm{diag}(\tau_i I_{(\tau_i \leq \alpha)})U^*$, the entries of $X$ may be assumed standardized and bounded by a multiple of $\log n$ and $\|T\| \leq \log n$. By Silverstein-Bai [2], $\|F^{Q T Q^*} - F^{Q T_\alpha Q^*}\| \to 0$ a.s. as $\alpha = \alpha_n \to \infty$.
nodes.statement_clean: Reduce to standardized X with bounded entries and bounded ||T|| via successive truncations/centralizations.

nodes.name: Tightness and Positivity of $\delta = \inf_n \mathrm{Im}\,\underline{m}_n(z)$
nodes.statement: By Silverstein-Bai [2], the sequence $\{F^{\underline{B}_n}\}$ is almost surely tight; therefore $\delta = \inf_n \mathrm{Im}\, \underline{m}_n(z) \geq \inf_n \int \frac{v\, dF^{\underline{B}_n}(\lambda)}{2(\lambda^2 + u^2) + v^2} > 0$ almost surely.
nodes.statement_clean: Tightness of {F^{underline-B_n}} implies a positive uniform lower bound delta on Im underline-m_n(z).

nodes.name: Apply Resolvent Identity (2.1) to Decompose $I + z(B_n - zI)^{-1}$
nodes.statement: Set $q_j = (1/\sqrt{n})X_{\cdot j}$, $r_j = (1/\sqrt{N})T^{1/2} X_{\cdot j}$, $B_{(j)} = B_n - r_j r_j^*$. Writing $B_n - zI + zI = \sum_j r_j r_j^*$, taking inverse on the right and using (2.1) gives $I + z(B_n - zI)^{-1} = \sum_{j=1}^N \frac{1}{1 + r_j^*(B_{(j)} - zI)^{-1} r_j}\, r_j r_j^* (B_{(j)} - zI)^{-1}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Use the rank-one resolvent identity to write a sum decomposition for I + z(B_n - zI)^{-1}.

nodes.name: Trace and Derive Equation (2.2) for $\underline{m}_n(z)$
nodes.statement: Taking trace, dividing by $N$, and combining with (1.2): $\underline{m}_n(z) = -\frac{1}{N}\sum_{j=1}^N \frac{1}{z(1 + r_j^*(B_{(j)} - zI)^{-1} r_j)}$ (equation (2.2)). Also $|z(1 + r_j^*(B_{(j)} - zI)^{-1} r_j)|^{-1} \leq 1/v$ (equation (2.3)).
nodes.statement_clean: Derive equation (2.2) expressing underline-m_n(z) as an average and bound (2.3).

nodes.name: Derive Equation (2.4) Linking $\frac{1}{n}\mathrm{tr}\,(-z\underline{m}_n T_n - zI)^{-1}$ to $\underline{m}_n$
nodes.statement: Writing $B_n - zI - (-z\underline{m}_n(z) T_n - zI) = \sum_j r_j r_j^* - (-z\underline{m}_n(z))T_n$, taking inverses and using (2.1)-(2.2), then trace and divide by $n$: $\frac{1}{n}\mathrm{tr}\,(-z\underline{m}_n(z) T_n - zI)^{-1} - \underline{m}_n(z) = \frac{1}{N}\sum_{j=1}^N \frac{d_j}{z(1 + r_j^*(B_{(j)} - zI)^{-1} r_j)}$ where $d_j = q_j^* T^{1/2}(B_{(j)} - zI)^{-1}(\underline{m}_n(z) T_n + I)^{-1} T^{1/2} q_j - \frac{1}{n}\mathrm{tr}\,(\underline{m}_n T_n + I)^{-1} T_n (B_n - zI)^{-1}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Equation (2.4): the trace identity expressed via per-column residuals d_j.

nodes.name: Bound $|d_j|$ via Lemmas 2.1-2.3 and Equations (2.5)-(2.6)
nodes.statement: Using condition (3), Lemma 2.1, Lemma 2.3 (a), independence of $q_j$ from $B_{(j)}$ and $\underline{m}_{(j)}(z)$, and $\|(A-zI)^{-1}\|\leq 1/v$ for Hermitian $A$: $E|\|q_j\|^2 - 1|^6 \leq K\, 6\log^{12} n / n^3$ and a similar sixth-moment bound on the analogous quadratic-form deviation. Combined with (2.5) $\max_{j\leq N} \log^p n\,|\underline{m}_n(z) - \underline{m}_{(j)}(z)| \to 0$, and Lemmas 2.2, 2.3 (b), (c): $\max_{j\leq N} |d_j| \to 0$ almost surely.
nodes.statement_clean: Apply concentration and resolvent inequalities to obtain max_j |d_j| -> 0 a.s.

nodes.name: Limit: $\frac{1}{n}\mathrm{tr}\,(-z\underline{m}_n T_n - zI)^{-1} - \underline{m}_n(z) \to 0$
nodes.statement: Combining (2.3), (2.4), and $\max_j|d_j| \to 0$: $\frac{1}{n}\mathrm{tr}\,(-z\underline{m}_n(z) T_n - zI)^{-1} - \underline{m}_n(z) \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$ almost surely.
nodes.statement_clean: Conclude that the trace residual on the left goes to zero almost surely.

nodes.name: Subsequence Limit and Uniqueness in $D_c$
nodes.statement: Pick a subsequence $\{n_i\}$ on which $\{\underline{m}_{n_i}(z)\}$ converges to some $\underline{m}$; let $m = -\frac{(1-c)}{z} + c\underline{m}$. Then $\mathrm{Im}\,\underline{m} \geq \delta$ so $m \in D_c$. Bounds $|1/(m'\tau + 1)| \leq |m'|/\mathrm{Im}\, m'$ and $|\tau/(m'\tau + 1)| \leq 1/\mathrm{Im}\, m'$ show $f(\tau) = 1/(m\tau + 1)$ is bounded with $|1/(\underline{m}_{n_i}(z)\tau + 1) - f(\tau)| \leq (|m|/\delta^2)|\underline{m}_{n_i}(z) - \underline{m}|$. Hence $\frac{1}{n}\mathrm{tr}\,(-z\underline{m}_{n_i}(z)T_n - zI)^{-1} = -\frac{1}{z}\int \frac{1}{\underline{m}_{n_i}\tau + 1}\, dF^{T_{n_i}}(\tau) \to -\frac{1}{z}\int \frac{1}{\underline{m}\tau + 1}\, dH(\tau)$, so $m$ satisfies (1.4); by uniqueness in $D_c$, $\underline{m}_n(z) \to \underline{m}$, hence $F^{B_n} \to F$ in distribution a.s.
nodes.statement_clean: Extract a convergent subsequence, identify the limit as the unique solution of (1.4) in D_c, and conclude convergence of the full sequence.

nodes.name: Yin's Real-Case Limit Theorem
nodes.statement: Assuming entries of $X$ and $T$ real, if $n,N \to \infty$ with $n/N \to c > 0$ and the moments of $F^T$ converge a.s. to those of a nonrandom p.d.f. $H$ satisfying the Carleman sufficiency condition, then with probability one $F^{(1/N)XX^* T} \to F$ in distribution to a nonrandom p.d.f. $F$.
nodes.statement_clean: Yin (1986) real-case limiting spectral distribution result, proved via the method of moments.

nodes.name: Marcenko-Pastur Limit Theorem
nodes.statement: For matrices $A + (1/N)X^* T X$ under finite-fourth-moment and mild dependence conditions on $X$, $T = \mathrm{diag}(\tau_1,\dots,\tau_n)$ with $\tau_i$ i.i.d. having p.d.f. $H$ on $\mathbb{R}$, and $A$ nonrandom Hermitian with $F^A$ converging vaguely: in probability $F^{(1/N)X^* T X}(x) \to \underline{F}(x)$ for all $x \neq 0$, where $m_{\underline{F}}$ solves equation (1.1).
nodes.statement_clean: The original Marcenko-Pastur result on (1/N)X*TX with A=0 and i.i.d. tau_i, identifying the limit via (1.1).

nodes.name: Silverstein-Bai Strong Convergence (Diagonal $T$)
nodes.statement: Under the assumptions on $X$ given in this paper and with $T$ diagonal, strong (almost sure) convergence of $F^{(1/N)X^* T X}$ to $\underline{F}$ holds with no restriction on $\{\tau_1,\dots,\tau_n\}$ other than its e.d.f. converging in distribution to $H$ almost surely.
nodes.statement_clean: Silverstein-Bai (1995) strong convergence result for diagonal T, the basis on which the present paper builds.

nodes.name: Stieltjes Transform Reveals Analytic Behavior of $F$
nodes.statement: Equation (1.1) reveals much of the analytic behavior of $\underline{F}$, and consequently $F$ (Silverstein and Choi [3]); even when $H$ has all moments, little information about $F$ can be extracted from the explicit moment expressions in Yin [4].
nodes.statement_clean: Justification for using Stieltjes transforms: they expose analytic behavior of F that moments do not.
